summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of renal transplant, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and moderate aortic stenosis was admitted for progressive dyspnea on exertion and atypical chest pain. Workup included a dobutamine stress echo, which was limited, and a low-probability VQ scan, ruling out pulmonary embolism. She underwent elective left and right heart catheterization, which revealed two-vessel coronary artery disease with a 70% stenosis in the mid OM2 branch of the circumflex artery. A bare metal stent was successfully placed. Hemodynamics showed moderately elevated left-sided filling pressures and moderate aortic stenosis. Lisinopril was uptitrated to 10 mg daily, and clopidogrel was initiated for dual antiplatelet therapy. Her transplant medications were continued without change. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans in cardiology and transplant clinics.
